newsitem.title: Malaysia: Consortium lays stone for Malaysian theme park.
newsitem.headline: Consortium lays stone for Malaysian theme park.

text.p: An international consortium laid the foundation stone for a 900-million-ringgit ($363-million) theme park in Malaysia on Wednesday and said it had already raised more than a third of the financing.

Former U.N. secretary-general Javier Perez de Cuellar, chairman of project developer Agarta Universe Sdn Bhd, said $130 million had been raised by international investors backing the project in southern Johor state.
Agarta is 90 percent owned by Ultrapolis 3000 Holdings Ltd Bermuda and 10 percent by a wholly owned company of Malaysia's United Malayan Land Bhd.
Ultrapolis is owned by a group of international investors.
Johor state chief minister Abdul Ghani Othman and Italian Deputy Defence Minister Gianni Rivera attended the foundation stone-laying ceremony on Wednesday.
The theme park is being built on 101 hectares (252 acres) near Johor Baru, Malaysia's second largest city, 20 km (12 miles) north of Singapore.
Italy's Advanced Development Attraction is producing components for the park, officials said.

Agarta Universe chief executive officer Rinaldo Romani said the park was expected to attract six million visitors a year, 90 percent of them from outside Malaysia. The park would need three million visitors a year to break even, he said.

Agarta would list its stock on the Kuala Lumpur bourse in five to six years after the December 1998 park opening, Romani said. He added that turnover for Agarta in the first year of the park's operation was estimated to exceed 350 million ringgit. ($1 = 2.48 ringgit)
